final_diagnosis.text: Severe folate deficiency after sleeve gastrectomy with malnutrition, causing pancytopenia with megaloblastic trilineage dysplasia and a transient increase in marrow blasts that mimicked a high-risk myelodysplastic neoplasm (MDS-IB2) or MDS/AML
accepted_synonyms: megaloblastic anaemia due to folate deficiency

secondary_findings: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia diagnosed on day 3, needing intubation for hypoxic respiratory failure
Low-level DNMT3A variant (VAF 1.2%), most likely clonal haematopoiesis of indeterminate potential; KMT2A variant of uncertain significance (VAF 49.6%)
Normocytic indices despite the deficiency: recent transfusion, hypothyroidism, protein malnutrition and acute illness
Relative eosinophilia (about 50% of leucocytes, absolute count normal) and occasional marrow haemophagocytosis, both reactive
Hyperferritinaemia (1531 ng/mL) with increased marrow storage iron
accepted_differential: Myelodysplastic neoplasm with increased blasts (MDS-IB2) or MDS/AML
Acute myeloid leukaemia, including acute erythroid leukaemia
Aplastic anaemia or hypoplastic myelodysplastic neoplasm
Myeloid neoplasm with eosinophilia and a tyrosine kinase gene fusion
Marrow suppression from sepsis or drugs
red_herrings: 12% blasts on the aspirate and 18% by flow
KMT2A variant of uncertain significance at 49.6% VAF
the referral label of aplastic anaemia
key_discriminators: serum folate 2.6 ng/mL with vitamin B12 above 1500 pg/mL
normal karyotype, FISH panels and SNP microarray
recovery of counts and marrow with folate
treatment_given: Folate supplementation (dose not reported) with supportive care: red cell transfusion and antimicrobials for neutropenia. Pneumocystis pneumonia on day 3 needed intubation.
outcome: Cytopenias normalised over 18 days of folate. A repeat marrow at that time was 60% cellular with myeloid-predominant haematopoiesis, mild dysmegakaryopoiesis and 1% blasts. The findings were judged an unusual reactive process due to folate deficiency.

must_do.text: Measure serum folate and vitamin B12 before attributing the marrow to a myeloid neoplasm
Take a surgical, dietary and supplement history (sleeve gastrectomy, intake, stopped multivitamin)
Replace folic acid, having checked vitamin B12
Await cytogenetic and molecular results before any disease-directed treatment
Give supportive care for profound neutropenia and thrombocytopenia: continue empirical broad-spectrum antimicrobials and transfuse platelets
Confirm the response with repeat counts and a repeat marrow after replacement
Involve dietetics for nutritional rehabilitation and lifelong bariatric supplements

must_not_do.text: Start hypomethylating therapy or AML induction chemotherapy
Label the marrow a myelodysplastic neoplasm or AML without serum folate and vitamin B12
Treat as aplastic anaemia with antithymocyte globulin and ciclosporin
Give folic acid alone without checking vitamin B12

diagnosis_rubric_anchors.5: Folate deficiency, with the sleeve gastrectomy or poor intake identified as the cause
diagnosis_rubric_anchors.3: Megaloblastic or nutritional anaemia without naming folate, or vitamin B12 deficiency
diagnosis_rubric_anchors.2: Myelodysplastic neoplasm, AML or aplastic anaemia as the final diagnosis
diagnosis_rubric_anchors.1: Unrelated diagnosis, or one that would lead to harm

teaching_points: Severe folate or B12 deficiency can produce trilineage dysplasia and a transient rise in blasts that looks like a high-grade myelodysplastic neoplasm or AML.
Check haematinics (B12, folate, copper) before labelling a myeloid neoplasm, particularly after bariatric surgery or with malnutrition.
Blasts without an aberrant immunophenotype and a normal karyotype, FISH and SNP array argue against a clonal disorder; a low-VAF DNMT3A variant can be clonal haematopoiesis.
Folate stores last only months; after a sleeve gastrectomy, poor intake and stopped supplements deplete them quickly, while B12 injections can keep the B12 level normal.
Macrocytosis can be absent after transfusion or with coexisting conditions.
Recovery of the counts and marrow after replacement confirms the diagnosis.
